topic: AI is redefining the firm itself
angle: AI value comes from redesigning operating assumptions, not sprinkling tools on old org charts.
sourceTitle: AI isn’t changing how companies work. It’s changing what a company is
linkedinPost:
AI doesn’t just change workflows. It changes the shape of the company that runs them.

A recent piece in Fortune argues the winners will abandon assumptions built for a world where intelligence was scarce and action was slow. That matches what I see as a Forward Deployed Engineer.

Most AI programs try to bolt assistants onto yesterday’s org chart. They reduce ticket time but keep the same swim lanes, approvals, and handoffs. You get incremental gains—and persistent bottlenecks.

The companies creating outsized value are redesigning the operating model: fewer queues, more straight‑through decisions, smaller teams owning outcomes end‑to‑end, and KPIs that measure flow (time to resolution, first‑contact success) instead of activity volume.

My take: AI ROI shows up when you delete work, not when you decorate it. Start with one customer journey and ask, “If competent judgment was abundant and instant, what steps disappear?” Then rewire policy, permissions, and incentives to match.

If your AI roadmap didn’t change org boundaries, decision rights, or metrics, you likely automated the status quo. Where would you redraw the lines first? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy #DigitalTransformation
